headline: Nvidia has promised computing power worth $250 million over five years to help British researchers study the safety and security of AI agents.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large named commitment backed by UK government quotes, but it is computing access rather than cash and key terms are still to be agreed.
importance_line: British AI safety researchers would gain computing power they would otherwise have to pay for, and the work is meant to produce safeguards for AI agents, but the value is in computing time, not cash, and Nvidia says the provider, technical design and commercial terms are still to be agreed.
summary: Nvidia says in a press release that it will donate computing access valued at $250 million over five years, or $50 million a year, for UK research on the safety and security of AI agents, mostly for the wider UK research community and in part for labs led by the University of Oxford and University College London and for Imperial College London. Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and chief executive, said the donation will let UK researchers "develop, test and strengthen safeguards" for powerful AI, and Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI minister, called it "a vote of confidence" in British AI safety research.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); text read in Nvidia's own press release, so the source is credited to Nvidia and Reuters is named only here. The $250 million is a compute donation 'valued at' that sum, not cash.
